subject: Governance sprint: ISO 27001 timeline & FedRAMP control gating
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orionfin.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orionfin.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Governance sprint: ISO 27001 timeline & FedRAMP control gating

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the overview last week. As we prepare our vendor intake, we need to align on two interlocking items before our procurement/infosec board meets next Friday:

1) ISO 27001 pathway — high-level timeline and the list of controls you will certify against (or plan to) in the next 9–12 months.
2) FedRAMP readiness gating — which controls require additional evidence (e.g., continuous monitoring, enclave separation, KMS attestation) and any required third-party attestations we should surface to our security council.

Can you share: a) a short milestone timeline with owners and b) the sample window(s) you typically provide for log/retention artifacts for auditors? We also have a small SIG/CAIQ intake attached for your initial pass (Orion_SIG_v1.xlsx).

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute checkpoint this week. Procurement is keen to understand expected vendor support during our assessment window.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
Orion Financial

Attachment: Orion_SIG_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orionfin.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Governance sprint: ISO 27001 timeline & FedRAMP control gating

Sarah — appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Kim, Marissa and Aditya (info sec and compliance owners).

Quick plan we propose:
- Deliver a 1-page milestone timeline (ISO 27001 stages + expected audit window) by EOD Wednesday (owner: Kim).
- Provide a FedRAMP gating note that lists controls requiring attestation and where we can provide equivalent compensating evidence (owner: Marissa) by Thursday morning.
- Share our standard sample window policy and examples for logs/snapshots (owner: Aditya) in the same package.

Attachments: we will review the attached SIG and return a completed baseline CAIQ/SIG file and a short control crosswalk. For transparency, we may flag a few controls that require either dedicated private deployment or a dedicated capacity commitment (so procurement can see tradeoffs).

Action items for internal team: Kim — timeline and control list; Marissa — FedRAMP gating & third-party attestations; Aditya — sampling windows and snapshots + examples. I will coordinate the call with Sarah after we have the draft artifacts.

Adding our proposed milestone cadence and initial owner map. I attached a short control-ownership sheet for review.

Milestones (draft):
- Jul 07, 2027: Internal control mapping complete (owners assigned) — deliverable: control-ownership.xlsx (owner: Kimberly)
- Jul 14, 2027: Evidence collection sprint (sample windows captured, initial artifacts delivered) — owners: infra team + Aditya
- Aug 15, 2027: Gap remediation sprint complete (high-priority gaps) — owners: infra/security
- Sep 10–24, 2027: ISO external auditor window (target) — high-level only, subject to change

FedRAMP gating notes (short):
- Continuous monitoring (CM): sampling windows and retained metrics are typically requested — we will provide a 90-day sample and a log extraction playbook.
- KMS & key management: we can provide KMS control narratives and attestations for customer-managed key options; for HSM-backed attestation we may need a partner letter (third-party).
- Separation/enclave controls: certain FedRAMP high-impact requirements imply private deployment — we will call out these as options and the expected cost/commitment.

Attachment: control-ownership.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed to see at a high level. A couple quick clarifications:

- For the ISO external auditor window, will Redwood be able to support snapshot extraction (read-only) and a 48-hour designated responder during the audit window?
- For KMS attestations, is there an expected turnaround time if we request a partner/HSM attestation? Procurement also wants to see estimated cost delta for private vs hosted options.

We can do the 30-minute checkpoint Thursday at 10:00am PT if that works for your team. I included procurement on the thread so they can confirm.

Thanks,
Sarah

Thursday 10:00am PT works for us — I've reserved a 30-minute slot and attached the initial SIG/CAIQ draft (sig-caiq-initial.xlsx) plus the evidence-owner matrix CSV. Agenda: 1) confirm snapshot & responder commitment during audit window, 2) clarify KMS/HSM attestation options and expected timelines/costs, 3) next steps + procurement ask list.

Quick answers in advance:
- Snapshot extraction/read-only: yes, we support auditor read-only snapshot exports; we will formalize extraction playbook during the evidence sprint.
- 48-hour designated responder: we can commit a SOC/Eng on-call during the auditor window for critical asks (subject to contractual SLA language).
- KMS/HSM attestation: typical partner attestation lead time is 3–4 weeks once scoped; we'll provide cost deltas for private/dedicated options in the packet on Thursday.

Attachments: sig-caiq-initial.xlsx (xlsx), evidence-owner-matrix.csv (csv)
